Like the first two, it is designed as a standalone game. This time, players take on the roles of highly trained marines, entering the alien nest with strict orders and the most advanced tools available. But will they be well-prepared enough to face the unrelenting horde that awaits them? In Nemesis: Retaliation, players must survive against overwhelming odds and the possibility of betrayal at every step. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 The Map 4 Equipment Cards & Inventory 5 Game Round Structure 6 Player Actions Overview 7 Intruder Movement and Target Priority 8 Intruder Types 9 Game End Overview Nemesis: Retaliation is a semi-cooperative board game designed for 1-5 players, which focuses on emergent narrative and the tension of the action-horror genre. Each player assumes the role of a marine squad member equipped with professional gear. They are sent to a Facility infested with deadly alien life forms and tasked with a mission – yet their own goals may conflict with one another. In the end, there is one thing they must do above all: survive. Setup Players select their Marine (e.g., Officer, Heavy Gun Operator, Recon) by choosing from two classes proposed. Each character has a unique Action Deck and Starting Equipment. You can check Mission Task as well as your Private and Mission objectives before choosing your Marine. Next step is Support Equipment Draft. Each player, except Contractor, choose one item from 7 cards proposed. Finally, each player is choosing 4 Tactical Gear tokens (Ammo, Grenade, Oxygen, Medpack) and places them in their Tactical Belt. After that, each player draws 5 Action cards and Player 1 begins the game. Other steps, like placing Robot in Hibernatorium, preparing Intruder Bag, starting Corridors, etc. are handled by BGA automatically. The Map The Map in Nemesis shows a Facility which is divided into 3 Sections – A, B, and C. The Facility consists of Rooms, which are always placed in one of the 3 Sections. The Rooms are connected by adjacent Corridors. Characters may only be placed in Rooms, while Intruders may be placed both in Rooms and in Corridors. Each Section has its own Life Support System that may be either Active or Inactive. Changing the status of those systems is possible in Life Support Control Rooms which can be found in every Section. Each Section has its own dedicated Section Rooms (marked with “A”, “B”, and “C” symbol). All other Rooms (marked with “?”) are random and may appear in any Section. On BGA, you can check all the room, by clicking magnifying glass icon above the board. Rooms are connected with Corridors. As a result of Movement and other Actions, Noise markers are placed in Corridors alerting you of incoming danger. When you roll Noise value matching the number of adjacent Corridor with Noise marker, you may spawn Intruders, depending on the token drawn from the Intruders Bag. Note that Intruders move into Room and Corridors, when Players move only between Rooms. Corridors can hold up to 6 Intruders or Queen and 2 other Intruders (Queen counts as size 4). Room can hold unlimited Intruders. Empty Corridors may be Reinforced during the game. When a Corridor is Reinforced, the Noise marker from it is discarded and the Corridor is flipped to the side with "0" value shown. Noise markers won’t be placed on a Reinforced Corridor. However, Intruders can still move into such a Corridor. Note: Corridors leading to the Hibernatorium can never be Reinforce
